October to December is short-rains season in Kenya, and afternoon downpours can soak you within minutes on Ngong Hills, in the Aberdares or on Mt Kenya. This guide to rain jackets for hiking in Nairobi explains which features matter, how to read waterproof ratings, how to check a pre-owned jacket, how to get the right fit over your layers, and where to buy one in Nairobi.

Quick Facts

  • Best for: Day hikes and treks during Kenya's long rains (roughly March–May) and short rains (roughly October–December)
  • Waterproof rating: 10,000 mm or more suits most Kenyan hiking; 20,000 mm suits Mt Kenya and the Aberdares
  • Breathability: Look for 10,000 g/m²/24h or more if you hike steep climbs
  • Must-have features: Taped seams, adjustable hood with a peak, storm flap or water-resistant zips
  • Fit: Size up enough to fit a fleece underneath without restricting arm movement
  • Where to buy: Find rain jackets for hiking in Nairobi at Mountain Mall, 3rd Floor, Shop D39, Thika Road, Nairobi, or online with M-Pesa or cash on delivery

Why Do You Need Rain Jackets for Hiking in Nairobi?

Rain jackets for hiking in Nairobi matter because weather on the ridges and forests near the city changes fast. A sunny 8am start at Ngong Hills can turn into a cold, wind-driven shower by early afternoon, especially from October to December.

Being wet is not just uncomfortable. Wind on an exposed ridge strips heat from damp clothing quickly, and at altitude that can lead to dangerous chilling. The Kenya Meteorological Department's outlook for the current October–December season pointed to above-average rainfall over much of the country, so check the latest forecast on the Kenya Meteorological Department website before you set out.

Rain jackets for hiking in Nairobi also double as wind layers on cold summits. On Mt Kenya, Elephant Hill or Kinangop, a shell worn over a fleece keeps you warm at rest stops even when it is dry. Our guide to rainy season hiking gear covers the rest of a wet-weather kit.

What Should You Look for in a Hiking Rain Jacket?

When comparing rain jackets for hiking in Nairobi, look for a waterproof, breathable membrane, fully taped seams, a hood that moves with your head, and enough ventilation to stop you overheating on climbs. These four features separate a hiking shell from a fashion raincoat or a light windbreaker.

Waterproof and breathability ratings explained

A waterproof rating in millimetres (mm) shows how much water pressure the fabric resists before leaking. Around 5,000 mm handles light rain, 10,000 mm handles most hiking downpours, and 20,000 mm or more suits long days in heavy rain. Breathability, shown in g/m²/24h, tells you how much sweat vapour escapes; higher numbers feel less clammy.

Many thrifted rain jackets for hiking in Nairobi no longer carry their swing tags, so the membrane name on the inside label is often your best guide. Branded membranes such as Gore-Tex, eVent or a maker's own waterproof-breathable fabric all indicate a technical shell.

2-layer, 2.5-layer or 3-layer construction?

Layer count describes how the membrane is protected. A 2-layer jacket has a loose mesh or fabric liner, a 2.5-layer jacket has a thin printed coating inside to save weight, and a 3-layer jacket bonds the membrane between two fabrics for the best durability.

Hood, zips and vents

A good hiking hood has a stiffened peak and adjusters at the back and sides so it turns with your head. Check that the front zip has a storm flap or water-resistant coating, and that pit zips or mesh-lined pockets let heat out on steep climbs.

Which Rain Jacket Features Matter Most for Kenyan Trails?

For Kenyan trails, prioritise a waterproof rating that matches your altitude, a hip-length cut that covers your waistband, and tough shoulder fabric that survives a backpack. Fit and comfort under a pack matter more than the lightest possible weight.

Below 2,500 m, such as on Ngong Hills or in Karura Forest, lighter 2-layer or 2.5-layer rain jackets for hiking in Nairobi's nearby hills are usually enough. On the Aberdares and Mt Kenya, where rain can last for hours and turn to sleet, a 3-layer jacket with a high collar is worth the extra weight.

Pair your jacket with waterproof rain pants and waterproof leg gaiters on muddy days, and our guide to choosing waterproof rain pants for hiking explains how to match them.

Are Thrifted Rain Jackets for Hiking in Nairobi Worth Buying?

Yes, quality thrifted rain jackets for hiking in Nairobi are worth buying when the membrane, seams and zips are still in good shape. A pre-owned technical shell from a respected outdoor brand often costs far less than a new jacket and outperforms a cheap new raincoat.

How to check a pre-owned rain jacket before you buy

  1. Turn the jacket inside out and look for peeling or bubbling seam tape.
  2. Check the inner face for flaking, white patches or a sticky feel, which signal a failing coating.
  3. Run every zip, including pit zips and pockets, from end to end.
  4. Test the hood and hem drawcords and the cuff tabs.
  5. Look for small holes or abrasion on the shoulders where backpack straps rub.
  6. Try it on over a fleece and raise both arms to check the hem and cuffs stay put.

A jacket whose outer fabric soaks up water but stays dry inside is usually fine. That is called wetting out, and it means the durable water repellent (DWR) finish needs refreshing rather than the jacket being worn out.

How do you choose the right size rain jacket?

Size rain jackets for hiking in Nairobi to fit over your warmest hiking layer. Wear or bring a fleece when you try it on, check you can zip it fully, reach forward without the hem riding up, and lift both arms without the sleeves exposing your wrists.

Pro Tips

  • Pack it high: Keep your jacket at the top of your daypack so it is out within seconds when rain starts.
  • Put it on early: Zip up at the first drops; drying out on a cold ridge is much harder than staying dry.
  • Vent on climbs: Open pit zips and the front zip a little to cut sweat build-up.
  • Wash it properly: Use a technical cleaner, not ordinary detergent or fabric softener, which can clog the membrane.
  • Revive the DWR: Follow the care label; many shells regain their beading with gentle heat after washing.
  • Check before the season: Spray the jacket with a hose or shower before October to spot leaks while you still have time to fix them.
  • Store it dry: Hang the jacket loosely after a wet hike instead of leaving it balled up in your pack.

How Do You Care for a Hiking Rain Jacket?

Care for rain jackets for hiking in Nairobi by washing them when it gets dirty, re-treating the water-repellent finish when water stops beading, and drying them fully before storage. Dirt, sweat and sunscreen block the membrane and make a good jacket feel leaky.

Wash with a technical cleaner on a gentle cycle, rinse twice, then follow the care label for drying; many brands recommend a low tumble dry or a cool iron through a towel to reactivate the DWR. If water still soaks in, apply a spray-on or wash-in reproofer.

Frequently Asked Questions

What waterproof rating do I need for hiking in Kenya?

A waterproof rating of 10,000 mm suits most day hikes in Kenya, including Ngong Hills, Mt Longonot and Karura Forest. For Mt Kenya, the Aberdares or long days in the short rains, choose 20,000 mm or a branded membrane such as Gore-Tex, which handles heavy, prolonged rain and wind better.

Is a poncho better than a rain jacket for hiking?

A rain jacket is better than a poncho for most hiking in Kenya because it stays close to your body in wind and leaves your hands free for scrambling. A poncho covers your backpack and ventilates well, so it can suit flat forest walks, but it flaps and snags on exposed ridges and rocky trails.

Why does my rain jacket feel wet inside?

A rain jacket feels wet inside usually because of trapped sweat, not a leak. When the outer fabric wets out, the membrane cannot release vapour, so condensation forms. Washing the jacket, refreshing the DWR and opening vents on climbs solves most cases. Peeling seam tape or holes mean a true leak.

Can I use a rain jacket as a windbreaker on Mt Kenya?

A rain jacket works well as a windbreaker on Mt Kenya because the waterproof membrane also blocks wind. Wear it over a fleece or insulated jacket at camps and on the summit push to Point Lenana. A 3-layer shell with a high collar and a hood that fits over a beanie gives the best protection.

Final Thoughts

The best rain jackets for hiking in Nairobi are waterproof, breathable shells with taped seams, a proper hood and room for a fleece underneath. Match the rating to your altitude, check the seams and zips on any pre-owned jacket, and keep it clean so it keeps working.
